 Medical supply giant recalls hospital beds amid reports of 7 deaths
 Aparajita Chatterjee Mon, November 16, 2026 at 10:03 PM EST 6 min read MDLN 0.00% 
 Trade Medline on Coinbase Trading disclosure Trading disclosure

 Learn more You may not recognize the name Medline, but chances are you have encountered its products during a visit to a hospital, doctor's office, or medical facility. 
 From disposable face masks, examination gloves, and surgical gowns to exam tables, hospital beds, and mattresses, the Illinois-based company supplies products used in almost every corner of healthcare. 
 In fact, Medline is the world's largest provider of medical-surgical products and supply chain solutions, as indicated by its reported medical-surgical sales. It offers approximately 335,000 products and generated $22.9 billion in net sales in the first nine months of 2026. 
 The medical supply giant also made Wall Street history last December after launching the biggest U.S. IPO of 2025 and becoming one of the most closely watched new healthcare stocks. 
 Read more: Alzheimer's families just lost one of their biggest hopes 
 But less than a year after its blockbuster market debut, Medline is dealing with a potentially costly safety crisis involving one of the most essential pieces of medical equipment: patient beds. 
 The company has recalled all Medline-branded beds and associated rails, mattresses, and accessories after reports of seven deaths and 35 serious injuries linked to potential fire and patient entrapment hazards. 
 The recall is so extensive that Medline has decided to discontinue the affected product lines entirely. 
 Medline recalls beds following reports of 7 deaths and injuries 
 Medline initiated the recall on Oct. 14, 2026, citing risks that could lead to serious injury or death. 
 In a Nov. 13 announcement published by the Food and Drug Administration , the company confirmed receiving reports associated with 7 deaths and 35 serious injuries as of Nov. 8. 
 The figures represent a significant increase from the two deaths and 16 serious injuries reported as of Oct. 20 in an earlier FDA safety alert .

 The reports are associated with the identified hazards, although they do not establish that the recalled products caused every reported death or injury. 
 The affected products were distributed in the United States and Canada between 2011 and 2026 to durable medical equipment providers, long-term care facilities and individual consumers. 
 The recall includes: 
 Medline homecare beds 
 Medline bariatric beds designed for heavier patients 
 Medline long-term care beds 
 Associated bed rails and mattresses 
 Hand-control pendants, motor boxes, and other electrical components 
 Replacement parts, accessories, and bed-containing order packages 
 Story Continues Medline has published an eight-page list of affected product numbers so facilities, caregivers and patients can identify recalled equipment. 
 Why are Medline hospital beds dangerous? 
 According to the FDA, the recalled products present two major safety concerns: overheating electrical components and patient entrapment. 
 The electrical hazard involves components such as hand-control pendants, control boxes, and motors. 
 Under certain conditions, including excessive loading, jammed motors, damaged controls, exposure to liquids, or the use of unsuitable accessories, these components can overheat. 
 Overheating may lead to smoke, sparks, melting, burns, or fires, potentially exposing patients to serious injuries, including electric shock and smoke inhalation. 
 The second risk involves patients becoming trapped while using beds with accessories or rails. 
 The FDA warns that bed accessories, loose or unstable rails, and situations in which patients lie on hand-control pendants may create entrapment or suffocation hazards. 
 These risks are particularly concerning because the affected products are used by people who may have limited mobility or require assistance to get out of bed. 
 Medline recalls products after death and several reported injuries.SOPA Images / Getty Images FDA says some recalled Medline beds can remain in use 
 Despite the seriousness of the recall, Medline has revised its instructions to allow certain beds to remain in use temporarily while customers arrange repairs or replacements. 
 The company initially notified customers about the product removal and market exit on Oct. 14. However, on Oct. 24, after consulting with the FDA, Medline issued updated instructions to reduce disruptions to patient care. 
 Under those instructions, customers should: 
 Unplug affected beds immediately if no electrical adjustments are needed. 
 Connect the bed to an electrical outlet only when adjustments are necessary to reposition the patient, and unplug it afterward. 
 Never use extension cords to power the beds. 
 Have a second person assist with bed movement and operation whenever possible. 
 Avoid unauthorized repairs, modifications or adjustments. 
 The company says affected beds may remain in use under these precautions until they are repaired or replaced. 
 Medline has also established a repair and replacement program. 
 Certain beds may be eligible for repairs and customers whose equipment cannot be repaired may qualify for a replacement or a full or partial refund. 
 According to Medline, these remedies may be available for eligible products purchased within the past five years. Older products are still included in the recall and remain subject to the safety instructions. 
 Customers who purchased or received an affected bed through a medical equipment provider or distributor should contact that provider to determine eligibility. 
 Medline bed recall could cost the company $200 million 
 The recall also represents a substantial financial setback for Medline, which completed its initial public offering in December 2025 and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MDLN. 
 In its third-quarter SEC filing , Medline estimated that the recall and product discontinuation could cost between $50 million and $200 million. 
 The expenses are expected to be incurred during the fourth quarter of 2026 and throughout 2027. 
 The company said the final amount will depend partly on how many customers participate in the repair, replacement and refund program. 
 The potential financial damage extends beyond the immediate costs of replacing or repairing equipment. 
 In a Nov. 16 SEC filing , Medline warned that the recall could expose it to product-liability claims, additional regulatory action and reputational damage. The company cautioned that these developments could adversely affect its business and financial performance. 
 The warning comes at a time when Medline is still establishing itself as a publicly traded company following its record-setting IPO. 
 How to check whether your Medline bed is recalled 
 Patients, caregivers and healthcare facilities can check the affected model numbers and access the latest notices through Medline's official recall resource center . 
 Customers who bought equipment directly from Medline can contact its recall customer service team at 1-800-950-0128, option 7 , Monday through Friday, between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Central Time. 
 You can also reach the company at recalls@medline.com . 
 Anyone experiencing an adverse event involving affected equipment can report the incident through the FDA's MedWatch safety reporting program . 
 Consumers should follow the updated safety instructions even if their beds were purchased more than five years ago, as the recall applies to all affected Medline-branded products regardless of purchase date.
